content.user_title: Debug Neovim and LazyVim Configuration Issues
content.value_statement: Neovim and LazyVim errors can be hard to trace across plugins, keymaps, and Lua configuration. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through focused diagnostics and evidence-based fixes.
actual_capabilities: Classifies Lua errors, keymap failures, plugin loading issues, performance problems, UI issues, and LSP failures.
Provides headless Neovim checks for plugin state, options, mappings, and loaded modules.
Maps common Neovim error messages to likely causes and diagnostic paths.
Explains LazyVim, which-key, LSP, Treesitter, Telescope, and completion troubleshooting patterns.
Uses targeted user questions only when local inspection cannot confirm the cause.
Formats final answers with symptom, root cause, evidence, solution, and prevention.
limitations: Requires access to the user's Neovim configuration to inspect local files.
Cannot confirm visual behavior without user feedback.
Does not replace plugin documentation for every version-specific change.
May need installed tools such as Neovim, lazy.nvim, or jq.

use_cases.title: Fix a broken keymap
use_cases.description: Trace whether a missing key action comes from mapping registration, mode mismatch, lazy loading, or which-key triggers.

use_cases.title: Diagnose plugin loading
use_cases.description: Check whether a plugin is declared, loaded, configured, and compatible with the current LazyVim setup.

use_cases.title: Investigate startup lag
use_cases.description: Compare baseline and full startup timing to identify slow plugins, repeated loads, or expensive configuration files.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose My Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner troubleshooting for a visible Neovim error.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the neovim-debugging skill to identify the likely cause of this Neovim error: [paste error]. Ask only for missing details.

prompt_templates.title: Fix A Keymap
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate troubleshooting for mappings that do nothing or trigger the wrong action.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the neovim-debugging skill to diagnose why [key] does not work in my Neovim setup. Check mapping registration, mode, and lazy loading.

prompt_templates.title: Trace A Plugin Loading Problem
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced plugin troubleshooting in LazyVim or lazy.nvim.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the neovim-debugging skill to determine why [plugin] is not loading or not exposing [feature]. Build a short test plan before suggesting fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A LazyVim Regression
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced regression analysis after updates or configuration changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the neovim-debugging skill to investigate a LazyVim regression after recent changes. Compare symptoms, plugin state, lockfile changes, and likely breaking changes.

output_examples.input: My which-key popup appears for Space but not for localleader mappings.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: the issue is likely isolated to localleader trigger handling. Evidence should compare leader behavior, localleader value, and which-key registration. Solution guidance should focus on the which-key trigger configuration.

output_examples.input: Neovim startup became slow after updating plugins.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: compare minimal startup timing with full configuration timing. Evidence should identify slow plugins or repeated loads. Solution guidance should test rollback or adjust lazy loading.

output_examples.input: My LSP server is installed, but completion does not work in one project.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: check client attachment, filetype detection, project root detection, and completion capabilities. Evidence should separate server startup from completion source configuration.

best_practices: Start with the narrowest symptom and test the most likely cause first.
Use headless checks for objective state before asking the user for manual output.
Confirm that the proposed fix changes the observed behavior before closing the diagnosis.
anti_patterns: Do not run every possible diagnostic command before forming a hypothesis.
Do not assume a plugin API still matches old configuration examples.
Do not ask for broad configuration dumps when one targeted check can answer the question.

faq.question: Does this skill support LazyVim?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes LazyVim-specific guidance for extras, plugin specs, lockfiles, and common override patterns.

faq.question: Can it debug which-key problems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers missing popups, localleader triggers, mapping registration, and version differences between which-key APIs.

faq.question: Will it edit my configuration automatically?
faq.answer: No. The skill focuses on diagnosis and proposed fixes. Any file edits depend on the host agent and user permission.

faq.question: Does it need to run shell commands?
faq.answer: Some diagnostics use local Neovim or shell commands to inspect state. The commands are intended for Neovim configuration troubleshooting.

faq.question: Can it handle plugin update regressions?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests checking lockfile changes, plugin changelogs, and rollback tests to isolate update-related failures.

faq.question: What should I provide when asking for help?
faq.answer: Provide the exact symptom, the action that triggers it, any error text, and whether it started after a recent change.
